text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The leadership of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour party (LDLP) resigned on Saturday during a meeting of the LDLP council after a crushing defeat in recent elections.
- Lithuania's population fell again in September. At the start of November there were 2,700 less people than in January.
- Some 40 percent of petroleum sold in Lithuania was smuggled.
- The trade deficit after eight months was 2.25 billion litas. The country exported goods of 8.387 billion litas and imported 10.642 billion litas, the statistics office said.
- Foreign state debt was $264.6 per capita on November 1, the statistics department said. Foreign debt was $981.5 million.
- Lietuvos Dujos (Lithuanian Gas) intends a 66 million litas share issue and said it regretted that the law limited the amountof private capital in the company.
- Problem-hit Lithuanian State Commercial bank has not succeeded in overcoming its decline.
- The government changes have not affected the market for govrernment T-bills. Experts forecast that interest rates on securities will go down further this year.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas has no doubt on the need for an army in Lithuania but pointed out that only full membership of NATO can ensure the country's independence.
- 5.1 million tonnes of grain had been bought by end November, 40 percent more than the same period last year.
